translations.title: Translations & AI
translations.intro: OpenDeck is an open-source project made by one developer, with a lot of help from AI. Here's where AI was used, what that means for you, and how you can help OpenDeck feel natural in every language.
translations.codeBody: Much of OpenDeck's code was written with the help of AI. A person reviews, tests and ships every change, and all of the code is available on {link}.
translations.draftBody: The English text is written by hand. The other languages, both the interface and the starter packs, were first drafted with AI. That's how a small project can offer so many languages from day one, but a draft can sound stiff, pick the wrong word or miss how people really talk.
translations.draftBody2: So we don't pretend the drafts are finished. The table below shows which translations a native speaker has already checked. Everything else stays a draft until someone does.
translations.creditsBody: These people read translations string by string and put their name to them. Thank you! 💛
translations.creditsEmpty: Nobody has checked a translation yet. Yours could be the first.
translations.helpBody: You can help without writing any code. Go through a translation string by string next to the English original, fix what sounds wrong and approve it. We'll credit you here by name.
translations.banner: This translation was drafted with AI and hasn't been checked by a native speaker yet.
translations.bannerPartial: Some text in this language is new or has changed and hasn't been checked by a native speaker yet.
translations.packNotice: Some words in this pack ({languages}) were drafted with AI and haven't been checked by a native speaker yet.
translations.settingsLink: About the translations and how to help

review.title: Review a translation
review.intro: Read every string next to the English original and fix anything that sounds wrong. Confirm each section once you've read it, and after the last one you can approve the translation. Your name will be shown as the person who checked it, so only approve what you would stand behind.
review.account: Sending your review opens a prefilled GitHub issue, so you'll need a GitHub account.
review.upToDate: Everything in this translation has been checked. You can still read it all again.
review.placeholders: Keep the placeholders from the English text: {list}
review.pluralForms: Plural forms needed: 1 or {count}, separated by a vertical bar.
review.fluency: How well do you speak it?
review.approveLocked: Confirm every section to approve the translation.
review.submitHint: A maintainer looks at your issue, and a bot then turns your changes into a pull request.
review.copied: Your review was too long for a link, so we copied it. Paste it into the Review field on GitHub.
review.saved: Your progress is saved in this browser, so you can take a break and come back later.

sent.stepOpened: We opened a prefilled issue on GitHub in a new tab.
sent.stepCreate: Check the form, tick any required boxes and click “Create”.
sent.stepReturn: Come back here. This page finds your issue by itself.
sent.searching: Looking for your issue on GitHub…
sent.notFound: We haven't found your issue yet. It can take a minute to show up.
sent.unreachable: We couldn't reach GitHub to check. If you created the issue, you're all set.
sent.receivedBody: You can close this page now. A maintainer will look at it, and a bot then turns it into a pull request.
sent.approvedBody: A bot adds your review to a pull request. It goes live once that is merged.
sent.doneBody: Thank you! It goes live on opendeck.space with the next update.
sent.closedBody: It was closed without being merged. You'll find the reason on GitHub.
sent.manualBody: You can close this page now. We couldn't confirm the issue on GitHub ourselves, so have a look there if you want to be sure.

anki.label: Anki
anki.step1: In the Anki desktop app, choose File → Export.
anki.step2: Pick “Anki Deck Package (.apkg)” for one deck, or “Anki Collection Package (.colpkg)” for your whole profile.
anki.step3: Keep “Include media” checked so images and audio are imported too.
anki.step4: Upload the exported file or files below. You can add several at once.

quizlet.label: Quizlet
quizlet.step1: Open your set on Quizlet and click ⋯ (More) → Export.
quizlet.step2: Leave “Between term and definition” as Tab and “Between cards” as New line.

csv.label: CSV / TSV
csv.step1: Export or save your cards as CSV or TSV.
csv.step2: Put the front in the first column and the back in the second (an optional hint in the third).

json.label: OpenDeck JSON
json.step1: Upload a .json file you exported from OpenDeck.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.s1Body: OpenDeck is an open flashcard application built on the AT Protocol. It reads from and writes to your Personal Data Server. OpenDeck does not operate its own account system and does not store your flashcards, study progress, or profile on its own servers.
terms.s2Body: You sign in with an existing ATproto identity. All content you create, including decks, cards, study progress, likes and follows, is stored as records in your own repository under the space.opendeck lexicons. You may delete or export this data at any time using any ATproto compatible tool. You can view your raw records on {link}.
terms.s3Body: Most data on ATproto is public by default. Unless a record is stored in a permissioned Space, assume anything you publish can be read by others. OpenDeck lets you choose what appears on your profile, but this is a display preference and not a confidentiality guarantee.
terms.s4Body: Do not use OpenDeck to publish unlawful content or to infringe the rights of others. Because content lives in your repository, you are responsible for it.
terms.s5Body: OpenDeck is provided as is without warranty of any kind. Spaced repetition scheduling is a study aid and not a guarantee of results.
terms.s6Body: These terms may change as the project evolves. Continued use means you accept the current version.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.s1Body: OpenDeck stores everything in your own ATproto repository. We do not run a database of your flashcards or progress and we do not sell or share your data since we never hold it. You can explore your public records on {link}.
privacy.s2Body: Sign in uses ATproto OAuth. Tokens are handled entirely in your browser and stored locally. OpenDeck never sees your password because you authenticate directly with your Personal Data Server.
privacy.s3Body: To show your name and avatar, OpenDeck reads your public Bluesky profile. Account search uses the public AppView network. These are public ATproto endpoints.
privacy.s3Github: The translations page shows the GitHub profile pictures of the people who checked a translation. Your browser loads them directly from GitHub, which can see your IP address when it does.
privacy.s4Body: For offline support and speed, OpenDeck caches decks, cards and progress in your browser. It also remembers small preferences like your theme in local storage. This data stays on your device and can be cleared at any time.
privacy.s5Body: Study reminders are push notifications and are only sent if you grant notification permission. So they arrive even while OpenDeck is closed, our server (hosted on Netlify) stores your device's push address, your DID, your time zone and the reminder text, and reads your reminder hour and days from your public OpenDeck profile. Turning reminders off, signing out or deleting your data removes all of this information. No study data is involved.
privacy.s6Body: OpenDeck ships without third party tracking or advertising.
